title: CRISPR-based modeling of loss-of-function mutations in cancer stress resistance
author: Simeoni, Loukas, et al.
materials: SYTOX™ Deep Red Nucleic Acid Stain

steps.title: Induce Cas9 expression
steps.instruction: Culture Cas9‑expressing MEXF 2090 cells in complete RPMI (10 % FBS, 1 % Pen/Strep) in two 10‑cm dishes at 70‑80 % confluency and add doxycycline to a final concentration of 1 µg mL⁻¹ to induce Cas9.

steps.title: Prepare crRNA and trRNA stocks
steps.instruction: Resuspend the synthetic crRNA library (0.1 nmol) in 5 µL per well of 1× siRNA buffer (diluted from 5× Dharmacon siRNA Buffer with DNAse/RNAse‑free water) to make a 20 µM crRNA stock; separately resuspend 20 nmol of trRNA in 1 mL to make a 20 µM trRNA stock.

steps.title: Form crRNA‑trRNA complexes
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of the 20 µM trRNA stock to each well of the 96‑well crRNA library plate, incubate 5 min at 20‑25 °C for annealing, then dilute the crRNA/trRNA mixture with OptiMEM to a final concentration of 200 nM (total volume 500 µL). Aliquot 100 µL of this complex onto PCR plates and store at –20 °C for future use. Use only 20 µM stocks; diluted molecules (e.g., adding 500 µL of 200 nM trRNA to individual 20 µM crRNAs) give inefficient complex formation.

steps.title: Prepare transfection reagent and plates
steps.instruction: Prepare diluted DharmaFECT Duo transfection reagent at 0.3 µL per 10 µL OptiMEM for each well of MEXF 2090 cells. Set up new 96‑well plates according to the number of transfections required; fitness assays should be performed in at least triplicate for each condition (untreated vs treated).

steps.title: Assemble transfection mixes
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 µL of the diluted crRNA library into a new 96‑well plate, add 10 µL of the diluted DharmaFECT Duo reagent, mix gently and incubate 15‑20 min to allow complex formation.

steps.title: Add cells to transfection wells
steps.instruction: Retrieve the doxycycline‑treated Cas9‑expressing cells, trypsinize, count, and calculate the volume needed to deliver 4 000 cells per well in 80 µL of complete RPMI (with doxycycline). Add 80 µL of the cell suspension to each well containing the crRNA/trRNA‑transfection reagent mix; the final crRNA/trRNA concentration in the well will be 20 nM.

steps.title: Culture transfected cells to generate KO populations
steps.instruction: Incubate the transfected cells for 5 days, expanding as needed and maintaining doxycycline for at least 5 days; editing should be complete. On Day 7 the arrayed KO populations are ready for large‑scale fitness assays. Optimize the transfection reagent for MEXF 2090 (e.g., test Lullaby, DharmaFECT Set 4, DharmaFECT Duo, Lipofectamine RNAiMAX using LMNA‑targeting crRNAs and immunofluorescence).

steps.title: Acquire Incucyte images
steps.instruction: Scan each 96‑well plate on the Incucyte® S3 Live‑Cell Analysis System using whole‑well scan mode. Set acquisition times to 300 ms for SYTOX Green and 400 ms for SYTOX Red. Timing for this imaging and analysis phase is 1–2 weeks.

steps.title: Perform image quality control
steps.instruction: Using the default analysis settings (which usually give accurate nuclei masks; adjust cell‑size parameters if needed), manually inspect images and apply the following filters: (a) remove wells with visible cell clumps; (b) discard replicate outliers that differ from the two consistent replicates by more than three times their difference; (c) exclude KO populations whose fitness under unperturbed conditions is reduced ≥20 % relative to the plate median (to avoid artificial fitness inflation). In the referenced study, 68 genes were excluded for severe fitness loss, leaving 250 KO populations; 61 of 7 200 imaged wells (0.85 %) were removed, of which 53 wells (87 % of excluded wells) were due to clumps and 8 wells due to inconsistent replicates.

steps.title: Quantify normalized fitness and identify hits
steps.instruction: Calculate the stress‑to‑unperturbed cell‑count ratio at the assay endpoint for each KO and control population to obtain normalized fitness. Compute Z‑scores using Z = (χ − μ)/σ, where χ is the fitness of an individual KO, μ is the mean fitness of negative controls, and σ is their standard deviation. Define enhanced or reduced fitness as Z > 1.645 or Z < ‑1.645 (90 % confidence interval). A sample‑to‑control ratio of 2:1 is used, so multiple‑testing correction is not required. Finally, perform validation experiments on selected genes showing a range of stress‑resistance phenotypes.
